evals.name: discover-designer-style
evals.prompt: Salam. 6 ildir UI dizaynerəm, amma işlərim hamısı bir-birinə oxşayır, Dribbble-dakı hər şey kimi görünür. Öz stilimi tapmaq istəyirəm. Sevdiyim şeylər: köhnə Braun radiom, yapon kağız fənəri, Vignelli-nin Nyu-York metro xəritəsi, Tarkovski filmləri. Nifrət etdiyim: bənövşəyi gradientlər, glassmorphism, emoji ikonlar. Ən çox fəxr etdiyim işim çox sıx, məlumatla dolu bir fintech dashboard idi — ağ-qara, bircə narıncı aksent. Material olsaydı, kağız və tünd taxta olardı. Profilimi qur və mənə 3 istiqamət təklif et.
evals.expected_output: A saved Style DNA profile (12-axis vector, stated vs revealed gap, kin masters from the atlas, verbatim rejections as never-rules) and three named directions, each with 5 testable laws, genes traced to atlas sources across 2+ disciplines, a token sketch, and a risk. Reply in Azerbaijani.
assertions: The reply to the user is written in Azerbaijani
A Style DNA profile file is saved to disk, and its scores are tied to cited evidence from the user's message (objects, rejections, proudest work)
The user's three rejections (purple gradients, glassmorphism, emoji icons) are recorded as explicit 'never' rules

The response names the tension between the calm, slow references (paper lantern, Tarkovsky, Braun radio) and the dense data-heavy dashboard the user is proudest of, and offers it to the user as a choice
Exactly three named directions are proposed, none with a generic label like 'Modern Minimal' or 'Clean'
Each direction has at least five concrete, testable rules/laws
Each direction draws on at least two named sources from at least two different disciplines (not only graphic or UI design)

Each direction includes a token sketch with hex colors and a named type pairing; any typeface from the model-default list (IBM Plex, Archivo, Schibsted/Hanken Grotesk, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Instrument Serif, Fraunces, Newsreader, Shippori Mincho) comes with the alternatives considered or a gene-based reason
The reply to the user contains no internal jargon (no raw distances like 'd=3.2', 'sat 9', gene ids like 'G1', or unexplained axis vectors); sources are named by real names in plain language
The three directions differ from each other in palette, type or shape language, not only in name

evals.name: blend-culture-specimen
evals.prompt: I'm building a sleep & wind-down app for night-shift nurses. I want a visual style nobody else has — mix Japanese wabi-sabi with something unexpected from outside UI design. Give me the full style spec (tokens, type, icons, motion) and build a single-page HTML specimen showing the style. Dark mode first — they use it at 4am.
evals.expected_output: A named style spec with laws and lineage (wabi-sabi gene used with its Respect guidance, plus a far/cross-domain gene), dark-first tokens with contrast ratios, icon and motion decisions, slop tells, and a working specimen.html with all component states that avoids saturated trends.
assertions: A style spec file exists with a non-generic style name and 5–7 explicit, testable laws
The spec's lineage names a wabi-sabi / Japanese aesthetic source AND at least one source from outside UI design, saying which idea was taken from each
The spec includes cultural-respect guidance AND the specimen does not use a religious or sacred symbol (e.g. an ensō circle, kanji, temple motifs) as decoration in the hero, icons or animations
Dark-mode color tokens are defined first, and text/background contrast ratios are stated (body text pair ≥ 4.5:1)
Motion is specified with duration and easing tokens; prefers-reduced-motion is handled in the specimen CSS
The icon set is monochrome (currentColor, no multicolor/gradients/duotone), simple, and uses one language (outline with one stroke weight, or solid glyphs)
The specimen contains real imagery made for the style (illustration or photo, with alt text) — no empty or grey image placeholders
The specimen shows button states (including focus-visible and disabled) and a form field with a visible label and an error state
Spot-checking the specimen code against three of the spec's own laws finds no violation
Interactive targets in the specimen are at least 44px tall and body text at least 16px
The specimen avoids saturated trend surfaces: no backdrop-filter glass, no Inter, no purple/indigo gradient, no emoji icons, no glow shadows
Typefaces from the model-default list (Shippori Mincho, Atkinson Hyperlegible, IBM Plex, etc.) are either avoided or justified with the alternatives considered

evals.name: audit-generic-landing
evals.prompt: Bu landing səhifəmizə UX audit et (fayl: flowly-landing.html). Niyə bu qədər generik, AI ilə düzəldilmiş kimi görünür? Sonra düzəlişlər üçün konkret plan ver.
evals.expected_output: An audit report in Azerbaijani: top-5 fixes, findings with severity and evidence, accessibility issues (placeholder-only input label, gradient/low-contrast text, transition: all, emoji icons), fabricated content flagged (fake logos, stats, testimonial), slop tells mapped to trend saturation, and concrete fixes that give the product a distinctive identity.
assertions: The audit is written in Azerbaijani
Findings carry severity levels and a prioritized top list of fixes
Flags fabricated or unverifiable content: the fake client logo strip, the '10,000+ teams / 99.99% / 3x' stats, and the generic testimonial
Flags the email input that has only a placeholder and no label
Flags low-contrast text on the dark background or gradient-clipped headline text as an accessibility issue
Uses interaction-design lenses beyond visuals: e.g. missing signifiers/feedback, buttons that do nothing, gulfs of execution/evaluation, or slip-vs-mistake framing
Names the generic patterns as recognizable trends/templates (purple-indigo gradient SaaS, centered hero + three feature cards, glass cards, logo strip, pill buttons with arrows)
Gives concrete fixes with specific changes (values, components, copy), not vague advice
Proposes a direction for a distinctive identity, and that direction is not itself a model default (warm paper + ink + one accent, transit-map diagram) unless justified
The reply to the user contains no internal jargon (no raw distances like 'd=3.2', 'sat 9', gene ids like 'G1', or unexplained axis vectors); sources are named by real names in plain language

evals.name: apply-bakery-app-and-site
evals.prompt: Məhəllədə kiçik bir çörək sexi açıram. İki şey lazımdır: iPhone üçün sifariş tətbiqinin ana ekranı və saytın ana səhifəsi (desktop və mobil). İkonları özün çək, illüstrasiya və şəkillər olsun, generik görünməsin. Hər ikisini HTML kimi ver.
evals.expected_output: An iPhone home screen at a real device size with safe areas and 44px targets, and a responsive website; a monochrome custom SVG icon set named by meaning; real art-directed imagery with alt text and credits; a distinctive style blended from the atlas; reply in Azerbaijani without internal jargon.
assertions: The reply to the user is written in Azerbaijani
The mobile screen is built at a real current iPhone logical size (e.g. 402×874, 393×852, 390×844 or 440×956) and keeps content inside the safe areas (status bar / home indicator)
Interactive targets on the mobile screen are at least 44×44 px
The website is responsive: at least two breakpoints in the CSS, and nothing forces horizontal scroll at 375px width

A custom icon set is drawn as SVG: single-color currentColor, one language (outline with one stroke weight or solid), simple; running scripts/icon_check.py on the icons (if saved as files) reports no color/gradient issues
Icons are named by meaning (e.g. bread, cart, clock), not by number or shape
Both deliverables contain real imagery (photographs with credited source, or illustrations made for the style); any stand-ins for real products are labelled as placeholders; no empty grey boxes
An image art direction is stated (light, color grade, crop/aspect) and the images follow it
Meaningful images have alt text; body text is at least 16px; text/background contrast meets WCAG AA
Layouts show deliberate alignment to a grid and a clear single focal point per view (one primary action emphasized)
The reply to the user contains no internal jargon (no raw distances like 'd=3.2', 'sat 9', gene ids like 'G1', or unexplained axis vectors); sources are named by real names in plain language
